This section asks for measurements on 2–3 repositories but always clones to the same `/tmp/cg-cost/repo`; on a fresh workspace the first clone can fail because `/tmp/cg-cost` is not created, and subsequent clones fail because the destination already exists, so the requested sample cannot be collected as written.

**Severity:** medium

<sub>🤖 Was this useful? React with 👍 or 👎 </sub>

Fixed in 60e0030c (2 edits applied, one commit; pre-commit checks pass and the new command block passes `bash -n`).

Part of this finding did not reproduce and part did. `git clone` into a path whose parent folders do not exist works, because git creates the parents, so the first clone does not fail for that reason. A second clone into the same destination does fail, with exit 128 ("already exists and is not an empty directory"), so the measurement could not be repeated for a second repository. A failed clone was also not stopping the later lines, which would have measured the earlier repository's folder.

Part 3 now makes a new `mktemp -d` folder for each run, clones into it, and chains every step with `&&` so a failed step stops the rest. I ran the same chain logic locally against a small repository: two runs gave two distinct folders, and an invalid URL stopped with exit 128 before any later step. The real `codegraph init` and `codegraph status` steps were not run.
